response.consequence: After the first rebalance, a thread-queue-parallel consumer silently stops processing results while advancing committed offsets. This loses check-in results permanently.
response.explanation: The FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and passed to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy built by create_thread_queue_parallel_worker. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close(), terminate() and join() call queue_pool.shutdown(). That sets worker.shutdown, shuts down every queue and joins the worker threads. Arroyo closes the strategy on every rebalance or partition revocation, then calls create_with_partitions again on the same factory. The new strategy receives the same queue_pool, which is already shut down and has dead workers, and the factory never recreates it. In the new strategy, queue.put on a shut-down queue raises ShutDown. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches this as a generic Exception, logs it, and marks the offset as added and completed. The commit loop then commits those offsets even though the messages were never processed. The shared OffsetTracker also keeps state (last_committed, all_offsets) across assignments, so stale offsets from revoked partitions can be committed.
response.title: Factory-owned shared queue pool is shut down by per-assignment strategy close(), after which messages are dropped and offsets committed

response.consequence: After each restart or rebalance, the last processed message per partition is processed again, which duplicates subscription results. Partitions with offset gaps stop committing, so large amounts of data are replayed after a restart.
response.explanation: get_committable_offsets returns the highest processed offset (highest_committable), and _commit_loop passes it unchanged to commit_function (line 287). Arroyo's commit callback expects the next offset to consume (message.committable is offset+1). So after processing offset N, N is committed and the consumer resumes at N, reprocessing the last message of every partition after a restart or rebalance. Separately, the scan breaks at the first offset not in all_offsets. Real Kafka topics can have offset gaps (compaction, transaction markers). A gap makes the partition's commit stall permanently at the gap.
response.title: Commits last processed offset instead of next offset, and stalls on offset gaps
